methods.label: Check the two-digit multiples
methods.explanation:
List the multiples of \(7\) in increasing order. The two-digit multiples begin at \(7\cdot2=14\) and end at \(7\cdot14=98\), since the neighboring multiples are \(7\) and \(105\). The complete list is
\[
\begin{gathered}
14,21,28,35,42,49,56,\\
63,70,77,84,91,98.
\end{gathered}
\]
Only \(28\) and \(91\) have digits summing to \(10\). Their sum is
\[
28+91=\boxed{119},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: Systematically listing small multiples and adding their digits uses elementary arithmetic.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is identifying multiples of 7 subject to a digit-sum condition. Tens-and-ones knowledge supports reading the two digits, while multiplication gives the complete bounded list of multiples.
